content:
Iconic ’90s rock band Pearl Jam has drawn the ire of conservatives with a scathing condemnation of the immigration crackdown by Donald Trump’s Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency.

The legendary Seattle group shared with its millions of social media followers a photograph of a protest that erupted at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport this weekend following the detention of a father and daughter by masked ICE officers.

Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza and Sofia Hernandez Mejia were boarding an Alaska Airlines flight to California to attend a family baptism when they were detained, reported The Guardian.

The band captioned the image:

“It is heartbreaking and infuriating to watch the human toll of a system driven by cold cruelty. Seeing a family torn apart and dragged off a jetway right here in our own airport by masked individuals is unconscionable and we stand firmly against this kind of inhumane treatment. That’s why this election mattered so much. It showed we aren’t powerless or screaming into a void. Americans stood up, looked at the systematic abuse and what ICE is doing to our neighbors, and said, no more.”

The post prompted a backlash from conservatives, including former U.S. Border Patrol commander Greg Bovino, who was removed from the role in January after federal agents killed American citizens Renee Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis.

“It seems that Pearl Jam and many in the music industry, as well as Hollywood, choose illegal aliens over US Citizens. Hey Pearl Jam, illegal aliens don’t like your music, your culture, nor your activism- they see you as a treasure chest to plunder. Naivety on full display.”

Newsmax personality Carl Higbie, meanwhile, was among those who sought to draw a parallel between entering the country without proper documentation and attending a Pearl Jam show without a ticket.

It’s far from the first time Pearl Jam has riled conservatives.

In 2018, the band sparked controversy over a Trump-themed concert poster, while in 2016, lead singer Eddie Vedder mockingly referred to Trump’s penis during a performance of the song “Wishlist” at Madison Square Garden in New York City.
